title: Toyota revives Scion with a 25 mph KEI-01 kei truck built in Indiana
verification: News, rung 1 (Nov 10-11, 2026). The Verge article read in full (specs, 25 mph LSV cap, 600 lb, 660cc three-cylinder, $34M Princeton Indiana, ~50 jobs, 2H 2027 fleet pilot, 30,000 used kei imports since 2020, Scion discontinued 2016). Toyota newsroom listing confirms the Nov 10 introduction of Scion by Toyota, the KEI-01 and 2H 2027 arrival; Google News shows the same story from Car and Driver, MotorTrend, Road & Track, The Drive.

slides.headline: Toyota's new truck tops out at 25 mph.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: a Japanese kei truck (1983 Daihatsu Hijet), TTTNIS / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

slides.text: Toyota is reviving Scion, the brand it discontinued in 2016. The first vehicle is the KEI-01, a pickup about 11 feet long and under 5 feet wide.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: a Japanese kei truck (Suzuki Carry), TTTNIS / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

slides.text: Kei trucks are tiny Japanese work vehicles. More than 30,000 used ones have been imported to the US since 2020. Toyota wants a piece of that.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: a kei truck in Tokyo, Japan, Syced / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

slides.text: It has a 660cc three-cylinder gas engine. Four-wheel drive switches on with a button. The bed holds 600 pounds, and three sides fold flat.
The catch: it's certified as a low-speed vehicle, like a golf cart, so top speed is capped at 25 mph. The cabin is sealed, with heat and A/C. The steering wheel is on the right.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: a kei truck, Ash-M-Bishop / Wikimedia Commons, CC0

slides.text: Don't expect to buy one soon. It starts in the second half of 2027 as a fleet pilot for farms, campuses, cities and delivery. Toyota is putting $34 million into its Princeton, Indiana plant to build it.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: a Scion tC from the old lineup, Motohide Miwa / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

slides.text: The old Scion sold sporty cars to young drivers. The new one sells a truck that fits through a garden gate and stops at 25. Would you drive one?

caption:
Toyota's comeback car is a tiny truck that can't go faster than a golf cart.

On November 10, 2026, Toyota introduced Scion by Toyota, a revival of the brand it shut down in 2016. The first vehicle is the KEI-01, an ultra-compact utility truck.

Kei vehicles are built to Japan's light-vehicle rules, and they have become popular in the US. More than 30,000 used kei trucks have been imported since 2020, about 7,500 a year.

The KEI-01 is roughly 11 feet long and under 5 feet wide, about half the footprint of a full-size pickup. It has a 660cc three-cylinder gas engine, a continuously variable transmission, push-button four-wheel drive and a bed that holds up to 600 pounds.

Because it's certified under federal low-speed vehicle rules, the top speed is 25 mph.

Toyota is investing $34 million in its Princeton, Indiana plant, with about 50 jobs, to build it. It arrives in the second half of 2027 as a fleet pilot for farms, campuses, municipalities and delivery operators. Toyota says it may open retail sales later if demand is there.

Would you drive a 25 mph truck?

Source: The Verge, Toyota newsroom
